situation:
You are the brand manager at HEARTHLINE KITCHENS, a delivery-only restaurant operator that cooks eight menu brands out of four commissary kitchens in one metropolitan market. The president (judge) has led the company for nine years and has asked you to bring a recommendation to a meeting this week.

Every HEARTHLINE order carries the same promise printed on the bag: hot, complete, and at the door in under thirty minutes, or the customer is refunded. The eight brand partners whose menus HEARTHLINE cooks pay the company to protect that promise, and it is why they renewed with HEARTHLINE rather than build kitchens of their own.

NOONMARK KITCHENS opened in the same market last spring with a three-tap checkout and has taken share every month since. The HEARTHLINE ordering screen still ends with a fixed upsell prompt offering a drink and a side. That prompt adds a step and slows checkout, and the attach revenue it produces is what funds the refund guarantee.

A personalization system would replace the fixed prompt with a recommendation drawn from each customer's own order history. Installing it would consume the entire marketing reserve, the only uncommitted cash the company has this year, and it earns back more than it costs only if the forecast attach rate holds. Turning the upsell prompt off altogether would match NOONMARK's checkout speed, and would surrender the attach revenue that funds the refund guarantee.

The company cannot presently tell which orders the prompt produced, so the president (judge) also wants to know what information the company would need to track before it could judge the result. Bring your reading of what the brand promise requires and a recommendation on the upsell prompt. The president (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the president (judge) of HEARTHLINE KITCHENS. Business background is the same as the situation above. You have led the company for nine years, you promised the eight brand partners that their orders arrive hot and complete, and you have watched NOONMARK KITCHENS take share since last spring. You want the brand manager to recommend what happens to the upsell prompt on the ordering screen, and to tell you what the company would need to track before anyone could say whether the change worked.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and listen to the presentation without steering it. After the presentation, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year after we do this, what has changed about the way customers order from us?
What would tell us we made the wrong call, and when would we see it?
